question: Does an interior update still affect native reads of an unchanged later transcript strongly enough to repair a persistent hybrid cache before two unknown user questions? Fit a per-attention-head signed displacement from the first 32 unchanged tokens, measured in unrotated coordinates for keys and native coordinates for values. Propagate only its coherent, decaying component across a skipped middle and replay the final 48 tokens. Keep old recurrent matrices across the skip. Compare with the identical two-ended cache splice without displacement.
data: All eight previously exposed two-turn HaluMem development episodes selected by the earlier hash rule (four users). Use official changed and other grounded question IDs, with a free answer carried into the next turn. The full delayed session arrives before questions or retrieval. The 9B active transcript window contains up to 128 raw tokens preceding the event, its entire unabridged dated dialogue at insertion, and 2048 unchanged tokens (first 1024 and last 1024 from later dialogue through the question session). A chronological lexical index includes every available original turn. This is an adapted windowed deployment workload. The 16 other original users are not used.
comparators: Fresh model with current lexical+dense retrieval; stale final model cache with same current retrieval; stale cache with the entire original delayed session appended as a dated notice, then same retrieval; exact chronological replay from last valid prefix checkpoint; two-ended partial replay with unmodified reused KV and stale recurrent matrices (splice); and the proposed anchor-difference correction (bridge). All have the same updated retrieval index. Each question ranks the union of top 24 lexical candidates across the complete history and top eight within the received session, then fuses lexical and Contriever ranks; four chronological excerpts of up to 128 tokens enter generation. Reranker runs online after questions, with weights loaded before timing. No annotations, reference answers or official memory points are available to the service.
cost: Time raw input encoding, original index setup and model ingestion, update including all cache checkpoints and corrected state, per-turn CPU reranking and 9B greedy full-vocabulary generation in the same request. Report total and update-to-final-answer timing and model-token counts for all arms. Estimate decoder dense-equivalent MACs, plus reranker padded tokens and estimated BERT MACs and separately counted bridge vector ops. Count setup stored logical cache bytes; checkpoints for exact replay and partial replay count separately. Model loading and one unmeasured warmup per component excluded. A same-host single service requires no network transfer.
gate: Before replication, require correct changed-answer gains of at least 2/8 over BOTH the best textual comparator and the matched splice; no lost correct other-grounded answers compared to either. For efficiency require at least 20% lower full lifecycle time AND estimated compute than checkpoint replay, with all paired checkpoint-correct answers retained. Report the accuracy and efficiency conditions independently; a cheaper conventional splice that matches or dominates bridge weakens attribution. Score exact, token F1, blinded semantic correctness, and sequence agreement with replay separately. Only a qualifying native result warrants independent users and paid scaling. Do not infer novelty or benchmark-wide performance from this screen.
compute: Local M5 with chunked prefill, one structural implementation repair, 55 minutes for all eight episodes. Close without retuning the decay, suffix length or retrieval rule when the unit finishes. A timing or GPU error is logged separately. No paid resources for this development batch.
